commenti.body: Has anyone seen the 2022 Mexican film *Dos Estaciones*? If so, what did you think?

Do you think that big budget movies should keep the international audience in mind, when creating the script?

Let me explain:

In The Batman, one of the riddles is centered around "Thumb drive" (Thumb = USB pen, but also Thumb = the actual finger of one of the victims).

Problem is... the object is called "Thumb drive" in America, but (according to wikipedia), the same object is called "USB drive", "USB stick", "flash drive" or "Pen drive" everywhere else.

In my country (italy), where the object is called "USB pen/key" 99% of the time  the traslators had badically no way to explain this riddle to the audience, so they gave up and, in the italian version, batman just says "thumb... drive" (in english!), and he gets the riddle right away. Cue lots of confused people in my teather.

Now, i'm not saying that every movie should be made more "generic" and less "english-centric". There are movies that only work in a certain setting, and for most of the other product, there's always the work of the traslators after all (where specific brand like "Cheetos" became "snacks", specific sport references like "end zone" became "score" etc...)

But in case of wide-release, big-budget movies that actually centered their plot points on specific wordplay or word-cues (like the Batman or a murder mistery), should the script keep the international audience in mind? Or it's OK to have scenes that ONLY work with THAT word or THAT object, and leave the rest to the translator (regardless of the final understanding of the international audiende)?

no, i think consideration for international audiences is why studios make less outright comedy films nowadays because theyre worried the humour wont translate in other countries so they might not do well at the international box office

i think its okay if the audience doesnt understand that one line in Batman, its not massive to the plot or the film, the film conveys the general idea visually anyway and with actor body language

Hi everyone!  
  
In case this may be of interest, I have just published a new movie montage focused on reflections in films – in mirrors, water, or other reflective surfaces. I aimed to create a dialogue (including parallels, contrasts and responses), to an extent, between the scenes and reflections included.  
  
I had to leave 200+ clips on the cutting room floor (otherwise it would have been wayyy too long), and my aim was of course not to be exhaustive, but I enjoyed exploring some of these different uses and shots of reflections, and the emotions that they may help generate. I hope that some of you will find it interesting!
